candidate.educational_objective: Apply the cited evidence to recognize the uniquely safest or most accurate nursing response in the clinical situation tested by V2-Q0105.

options.A: Combined hormonal contraception is category 1 because smoking fewer than 15 cigarettes per day removes the vascular restriction after age 35.
options.B: Combined hormonal contraception is category 2 because migraine with aura is relevant only when hypertension is also uncontrolled or severe.
options.C: Combined hormonal contraception should not be used because migraine with aura is category 4, and smoking at age 35 or older adds further vascular risk.
options.D: Combined estrogen-progestin contraception is preferred because estrogen lowers stroke risk enough to offset the additional risk associated with smoking.

candidate.rationale: CDC U.S. MEC classifies combined hormonal contraception as category 4 for migraine with aura, meaning an unacceptable health risk. Smoking at age 35 or older adds additional cardiovascular risk; for fewer than 15 cigarettes per day, smoking alone is category 3 for combined hormonal contraception.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Migraine with aura: CHC category 4. Smoking age ≥35 and <15 cigarettes/day: CHC category 3.
